In all honesty, I enjoyed what this game offered to us, was it the Left for Dead 3 that it was hyped up to be? Not at all, Left for Dead 2 is such an amazing game by itself it stands as an all time classic for video games in general. But from my experience, I believe this game held itself up to it's standards, no single build is alike, you can make your character run sonic speeds with SMGs, a Melee build that just eats hordes and damage, or a copper loving build built to give all your teammates buffs with cards. All mutations or special ridden are unique while giving them all a certan class to originate. I do believe there is plenty of room for improvement possibly in the future updates involving PvP which could help boost this game to what it's full potential can be. But from a PvE standpoint, and how I mostly played this game, it was quite enjoyable.

After a bit of play and finally committing doing to doing a full melee run I want to throw in some feedback. For a start I'm not a great player and I don't play on the hard difficulty's, and mostly play solo or with my roommate so my scope is a bit limited.
As for melee, doing the hives early on felt like the edge of terror with some maniacal laughter added in and I often resorted to my M1A for specials. With a few more cards under my belt I seemed to hit the sweet spot and could take on almost everything without too much thought. With every card I got life got easier and by the end only Ogre's were an issue, and even then with enough normal ridden around I could just wade in swinging wildly. I got enough temporary health that most specials didn't matter, with the breakout card I could ignore most all else... but the game play just became run at anything that moves swinging wildly and win. Their was no tactics, no strategy, no finesse. It was funny, but after 6 maps in a row where that was all I needed to do, I was over 100 temp health above my default, had nothing to spend copper on it lost it's appeal.
So here are a few changes I'd like to put forward to make melee a little more engaging and a little less one dimentional.
1. For each level of a melee weapon increase it's base damage by a little less, but increase it's range by 0.25, or 0.5 meters. This seems like very little but taking melee range from 2 meters to 3 meters with a better weapon can change the way you handle things.
2. Reduce the amount of melee cards that add attack speed, and replace them with other melee style mechanics, like something that adds a block if you haven't sprinted or attacked for the last 4 seconds. Make the block like Sharice's armour to absorb 1 hit.
3. Buffs that increase your damage and other things shouldn't decrease visibility while holding a melee weapon. Sadistic for example did this and made life far harder to see what was going on, but I could still "win" by just swinging wildly.

I could probably thing of a few other minor things but I'd like end game melee to be a little more strategy and a little less frothing-at-the-mouth-stark-raving-lunatic style.
